title: Capacity fallout runway checkerboard
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet maps granular headcount triggers against pricing sensitivity scenarios and burst-capacity outcomes. The model is intentionally compact — a checkerboard view so product, infra, and finance can quickly scan tradeoffs when token demand or GPU availability diverges from baseline forecasts.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Base assumptions: $0.0007 per token avg (mix of embeddings + generation), avg serving latency target 150ms p50, and committed GPU pool cost $120k/month (net of discounts).
- If price per token compresses by >20% while throughput increases >2.5x, runway shrinks ~6–8 weeks unless we enact hiring and slab adjustments.
- Primary levers: temporary contractor pool, burst-credit reallocation, model quantization rollout (Q3 pilot), and soft hiring freeze for non-customer-facing roles.

Assumptions and inputs (editable):
- Revenue mix: 70% hosted API, 20% dedicated, 10% private.
- Token mix: 65% short-form chat (<128 tokens), 35% long-form generation (>512 tokens).
- Cost per GPU hr (effective): $3.10 (post-commit).
- Avg tokens per request: 220.
- Baseline monthly tokens: 18B.
- Baseline FTE cost burden (fully loaded): $220k/year/FTE (engineer), $160k/year/FTE (ops/finance/support).

Checkerboard matrix (scenarios):
Columns = Capacity state: Healthy (burst available), Constrained (burst reduced 50%), Fallen-through (burst exhausted).
Rows = Pricing shock: Price +10% (upside), Price 0% (base), Price -15% (mild compression), Price -30% (severe compression).

Matrix (high level outcomes):
- Price +10% / Healthy: Headcount plan -> accelerate hiring (2 ICs eng, 1 SRE), runway +8w. Action: open reqs, deploy quantization pilot later.
- Price 0% / Constrained: Headcount -> delay non-critical hires (product ops), reallocate burst credits to top-tier customers; runway neutral. Action: temp contractor for SRE on-call.
- Price -15% / Constrained: Headcount -> hiring freeze for 8 weeks, migrate non-latency workloads to cheaper model variants, runway -4w. Action: enable per-route cold cache, ramp Optimize recommendations.
- Price -30% / Fallen-through: Headcount -> immediate soft hiring freeze, evaluate 10–12% staffing reallocation (shift to contract), initiate emergency price floors for new customers, runway -10w. Action: trigger contingency committee, notify sales/CS.

Quantified quick sheet (illustrative numbers):
- Baseline monthly cost (infrastructure + infra labor): $1.45M
- Token price -15% with +30% usage -> monthly revenue delta: -$108k, cost delta +$320k -> net burn +$428k
- Headcount mitigation options:
  - Option A: Contractor surge (12 FTE weeks) cost = $96k (saves 4 hiring cycles)
  - Option B: Delay hires (3 FTE) for 12 weeks = immediate savings ~$165k payroll runrate reduction
  - Option C: Quantization full rollout (est. savings month 2) = 12–18% infra savings but upfront infra engineering cost 0.8 FTE-month

Trigger rules (operational):
- Metric feeds to watch (automated): daily token delta vs baseline (>10%), committed GPU utilization (>85% sustained 3 days), margin per route (<12% for 48 hours).
- If any 2 triggers fire within a 7-day rolling window -> move to Stage 2 response (freeze non-essential hiring, start contract engagement).
- If 3 triggers fire or revenue down >20% MoM -> Stage 3 (exec emergency, priced floor on onboarding, perform layoffs only as last resort).

Checklist (first 48 hours after trigger):
- [ ] Finance: Run updated three-scenario P&L (fast-mode) — 24h
- [ ] SRE: Re-evaluate burst credit pool and request temporary re-allocation — 24h
- [ ] Product: Flag non-customer facing feature releases that can be paused — 48h
- [ ] Sales/CS: Communicate potential short-term changes to SLA/burst availability for new deals — 48h
- [ ] People Ops: Stand up hiring hold communication plan and contractor ramp list — 48h

Headcount prioritization matrix (simple scoring):
- Score each req 0–10 on customer impact, revenue enablement, operational risk reduction, and time-to-value. Prioritize >=26 as green (proceed), 18–25 amber (defer/contract), <18 red (freeze).

Small checklist for pricing sensitivity tests (finance + product):
- Build synthetic cohorts: heavy-embedding, heavy-generation, mixed. Project net margin at -10%, -20%, -30% price points.
- Stress test model-mix shifts (e.g., 20% migration from hosted->dedicated) and compute QoQ impact on committed capacity.
- Run token serp tests: how many customers produce >500k tokens/day and are in top 5% of cost.

Open questions / Notes to self: 
- We need a rolling contract list (contractor name, skills, hourly cap) tied to People Ops budgets. Marco to own creation (JIRA-FIN-981).
- How do we instrument per-route cold cache economics? Need engineering estimate. Priya to follow up with APPLIED-ML (slack thread #quantize-runbook).
- Is there a small price-floor experiment we can run on new signups without breaking existing enterprise SLAs? Consider soft quota gating.

Version history and next steps: 
- v0.1 (2026-06-12) initial sketch and scenario grid (this file)
- v0.2 due 2026-07-09: add contractor roster and 3-scenario P&L workbook (linked artifact)
- Next meeting: finance+product deep-dive 2026-06-18 (prep: bring actual committed GPU hours for May/Jun and top 20 customers token mix).
